newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposes barring Sun-Diamond affiliates.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposes barring Sun-Diamond affiliates.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday said it has proposed barring certain officials and affiliates of Sun-Diamond Growers of California from participating in any federal purchasing programs after the fruit concern's recent criminal conviction.

"USDA proposes to debar Sun-Diamond's directors, managing officials, and affiliates because of their silence and failure to correct the criminal and dishonest business practices leading to the court conviction," USDA said in a statement.
USDA official Robert Keeney said the proposed debarment takes place at announcement, pending the debarred parties'submissions of information in their defense.

Sun Diamond was convicted in September in a federal court on eight criminal counts that included illegal gratuities to former Agricuture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994 and illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry.
In October, the Agriculture Department barred Sun-Diamond from federal food purchase programs for the next three years.

USDA said the affiliates it proposed to bar were Diamond Walnut Growers Inc, Stockton, Calif.; Sun-Maid Growers of California, Kingsburg, Calif; Sunsweet Growers Inc, Yuba City, Calif; Valley Fig Growers, Fresno, Calif., Hazelnut Growers of Oregon, Cornelius, Ore; and Sunland Products of California, Pleasanton, Calif.
The affiliates, who have not been named in any criminal indictments, rank as the nation's largest raisin, prune, walnut fig and apricot cooperatives.
USDA also listed 12 Sun-Diamond officials it proposed to exclude.

USDA said the individuals and affiliates have 30 days to appeal. It said the typical debarment is for three years and would be government-wide. USDA did not provide any data on how much the government buys from Sun-Diamond affiliates.
